newsitem.title: USA: Chubb's stock soars on report it may sell units.
newsitem.headline: Chubb's stock soars on report it may sell units.

text.p: Chubb Corp.'s stock shot up 12 percent Friday after it told Wall Street analysts in a private conference call a day earlier that it might sell its life insurance and real estate businesses.
Company officials confirmed Friday that the conference call had taken place, and a taped version was made available.
In the call, Chief Executive Officer Dean O'Hare said Chubb was considering the sale of its life insurance and real estate units to improve shareholder value.

Chubb's stock jumped $5.50, or about 12 percent, to $51 on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was one of the most active issues. Chubb, based in Warren, N.J., earns about 22 percent of its annual revenue from the life insurance and real estate operations.
O'Hare said the additional commitment needed to make Chubb's mid-sized life insurance unit more efficient and competitive with its much larger rivals "may not be in the best interest of shareholders.
"Therefore, we feel it necessary to again consider our options," O'Hare said. He said a decision might be made before the end of the year.
Proceeds from a sale of the businesses could be used to buy back stock, make an acquisition to gain entry into an international market or expand the company's other businesses, O'Hare said.
"Life insurance never really worked for Chubb," said Leandro Galban Jr., a managing director in investment banking at Donaldson, Lufkin and Jenrette.
The business has produced only single digit returns on equity, dragging down the performance of Chubb's main commercial and personal property-casualty business.
"They're so good at so many other things, but it's never been a front runner for them," he said. "It's not a bad company, it's simply a question of commitment."
A company with a greater focus on life insurance might find the business attractive, he said.
"I think it will probably attract a pretty large cast of buyers," another industry source said.
Bear Stearns analyst Steven Gavios said in a research report the life operations currently have equity of $842 million and the real estate operations have equity of $426 million.
He upgraded the stock to buy from attractive and has a 12- to 18-month price target of at least $65 a share.
"We believe the sum of the parts is worth $65 a share or higher," Gavios told Reuters.

"We believe that Mr. O'Hare's patience has run out, with the turnaround at the life operations happening slower than expected, which pushed out the waiting time until the earnings performance would be up to par," Gavios said in his report.

"Additionally, with the dramatic consolidation of the life insurance industry going on today, Chubb has come to the realisation that being a player in the life business would have required it to double down on its investment, which management did not think was prudent," Gavios said.
